doc: The one engine-authority rule set. Limen's own guardrails (scripts/check-architecture.ts via tools/guardrails/boundary.ts) and the consumer-facing `limen verify` (cli/Limen.Core/Boundary.fs, which embeds this file at build time) both read it; neither holds a token list of its own. test/boundary-rules.test.ts and cli/tests/Limen.Core.Tests/BoundaryRulesTests.fs run the same fixtures (test/fixtures/boundary-rules/cases.json) through both implementations, and the CLI reports this file's SHA-256 as `ruleSet.sha256` so a verify result names the rules it ran. Matching is lexical: comments and string literals are removed, then each token must stand as a whole word (a token ending in `(` is a call, whitespace allowed before the parenthesis). Guardrail-owned: change only under a guardrail-scoped work item.

engine.doc: Engine-side code holds application authority. It may not acquire browser, JavaScript-interop, network, filesystem or process authority; it requests effects and receives results.

moduleSpecifierPrefixes.doc: Import specifiers an engine may not load (checked against the specifier text of static and dynamic imports, which comment and string removal would otherwise hide).

dynamicTypes.doc: Ways to defeat the type system, which is how meaning crosses the boundary unnoticed.

everywhere.doc: Ways to hand the browser something to execute. Banned on both sides of the boundary, in every language.
